Embellish

em-BEL-ish · verb

Hear It

What It Means

To embellish is to make something more attractive by adding decorative details; also, to make an account or story more interesting by adding extra, often invented details.

The tailor embellished the plain black jacket with hand-stitched silver thread along the collar.

Worked Example

The birthday planner embellished the plain cardboard sign with glitter, ribbon, and paper flowers until it barely looked handmade.

The sign didn't start out fancy at all -- glitter, ribbon, and paper flowers were added to dress it up, which is exactly what it means to embellish something.

How Embellish Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

ornament

ornament: to decorate with extra details

dramatize

dramatize: to present something in a more vivid or exciting way than it really is

Antonyms

simplify

simplify: to make plainer or less complicated

understate

understate: to describe something as smaller or less important than it really is

How Strong Is It? — touch up → embellish → overdo

touch up vs. embellish

touch up vs. embellish: Touching up is lighter than embellishing: a touch-up makes one small, quiet improvement, while to embellish is to layer on decorative detail after decorative detail.

overdo vs. embellish

overdo vs. embellish: To overdo something means adding so much that it becomes too much, taking embellishment a step too far.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — em-

prefix — em-: to put into a certain state (French/Latin en-)

root — bel / beau

root — bel / beau: beautiful (Latin bellus)

suffix — -lish

suffix — -lish: the -ish verb ending (the l doubles) (French)

Put it together

Put it together: Embellish comes from Old French embellir -- em- ('to put into a state') plus bel ('beautiful,' from Latin bellus) plus the -ish verb ending, as in finish, with the l doubled. The same Latin root gives us beauty: to embellish something is literally to make it more beautiful.

Use the root in a new word: beauty

Use the root in a new word: beauty: The old barn had a rustic beauty that no amount of fresh paint could improve.
